Actually, you lose X life regardless of who you target — the life loss is the same. So the choice of target doesn't matter when all graveyards have the same number of creature cards (1). This is actually not a blunder.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted themselves for Corpse Augur trigger
annotations.betterLine: Any target gives the same result (X=1), so this is fine

annotations.description: Playing Temple of the False God as the 7th land is fine for mana, but Forest or Mountain would have been better here. With 6 lands already (including Rakdos Carnarium which taps for BR), playing Forest would allow casting Explosive Vegetation this turn (3G = Forest + 3 other lands), which would ramp significantly and set up Rampaging Baloths landfall triggers next turn. Temple of the False God enters tapped and doesn't help this turn. Alternatively, playing Mountain + Forest (wait, only one land drop) - but the key issue is that with the current mana base (Swamp, Rakdos Carnarium for BR, 3 Forests), playing Forest gives access to 4 green sources + 2 other = 6 mana including 3G needed for Explosive Vegetation. Playing Temple of the False God enters tapped so it produces nothing this turn, whereas a basic land could enable Explosive Vegetation immediately, which fetches two more basics and accelerates toward Thantis or Rampaging Baloths much faster.

annotations.betterLine: Fetch a Mountain and a Swamp (or at least one of them) to improve mana redundancy for Thantis and Gaze of Granite, ensuring they can cast their spells even if Rakdos Carnarium is removed.

annotations.description: Bloodtracker is a 3/3 flyer with +1/+1 counters that draws cards when it leaves the battlefield. Attacking with it in a 4-player game exposes it to potential blockers or removal, risking losing the card draw trigger prematurely. With only one creature on the board, sending it into combat provides minimal pressure (3 damage to one opponent) while risking the creature. Additionally, Bloodtracker's value increases over time as more +1/+1 counters are added (especially with proliferate effects or paying life), so keeping it back to grow is often better. However, the only creature available is Bloodtracker, and 'All attack' is the same as attacking with just Bloodtracker, so the decision is really about whether to attack at all. With no blockers obviously threatening and wanting to apply pressure, attacking is reasonable.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Bloodtracker 3/3
annotations.betterLine: This is debatable - attacking with a growing Bloodtracker is fine if no dangerous blockers are present, but holding back to continue growing it could yield more value long-term.

annotations.betterLine: Play Golgari Guildgate (enters tapped) this turn since 5 untapped mana is sufficient for current castable spells, saving Command Tower for a future turn when the extra untapped mana and flexibility matters more.

annotations.description: Gem3Flash equipped Lightning Greaves to Meren of Clan Nel Toth before playing their land for the turn. They have Slippery Karst (enters tapped), Golgari Guildgate (enters tapped), and Forest in hand. Playing a land first is free and should be done before spending any actions. While the equip costs 0 mana, playing the land first is strictly better sequencing — it gives more information and ensures the land drop isn't forgotten. More importantly, equipping Greaves to Meren gives it shroud, which means Meren can't be targeted by your own spells/abilities if needed. The Greaves equip could wait until after other main phase actions. Additionally, with Meren's end step trigger requiring you to target a creature card in your graveyard, having Greaves on Meren is fine, but the sequencing of land before equip is a minor error.
annotations.actionTaken: Equipped Lightning Greaves to Meren before playing a land
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first (Forest for untapped mana, or Golgari Guildgate/Slippery Karst if saving the Forest), then equip Lightning Greaves to Meren

annotations.description: Gem3Flash is discarding to hand size at end of turn. Spider Spawning creates tokens based on creature cards in the graveyard, and with Meren of Clan Nel Toth as commander (which rewards creatures dying and can recur creatures), Spider Spawning could be a strong late-game card. However, discarding it to the graveyard does give it flashback access ({6}{B}), so it's not entirely lost. The alternative considerations: Golgari Guildgate is a tapped land that's relatively low-value with 7 lands already in play. Forest is also somewhat replaceable. Eater of Hope at 7 mana is very expensive and the board doesn't have many sacrifice fodder creatures yet. The discard of Spider Spawning is defensible since it retains flashback value, but discarding the Golgari Guildgate (a tapped land when you already have 7 lands including color fixing) would preserve more options while losing less strategic value.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Spider Spawning
annotations.betterLine: Discard Golgari Guildgate - with 7 lands already in play including Command Tower and Vivid Marsh for color fixing, the tapped land is the lowest-impact card. While Spider Spawning has flashback, keeping it in hand preserves the option to cast it at its cheaper regular cost (4G vs 6B for flashback).

annotations.description: Gem3Flash cast Corpse Augur before playing a land. They have Forest and Golgari Guildgate in hand but only played one land so far this turn. Playing a land first (Forest) would give access to more mana this turn or in future turns. Additionally, Wood Elves would be a stronger play here as it ramps by fetching a Forest to the battlefield, and with Meren on the field, the 1/1 body is excellent fodder for experience counters. Wood Elves costs 2G vs Corpse Augur's 3B, so after playing Forest they'd have the same mana available. More importantly, casting Corpse Augur now is questionable value - it's a 4/2 that draws cards when it dies based on creatures in a graveyard, but you'd want to time its death carefully. Wood Elves provides immediate ramp value and synergizes better with Meren.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Corpse Augur before playing a land for turn
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest first, then cast Wood Elves to ramp (fetching another Forest), building toward casting expensive threats like Pathbreaker Ibex or Eater of Hope sooner while generating Meren synergy

annotations.description: Equipping Lightning Greaves to Meren (the only creature) before playing a land or casting spells is poor sequencing. Meren already has shroud from the Greaves being equipped, and re-equipping to the same creature accomplishes nothing. More importantly, the player should play their land drop first (Forest or Golgari Guildgate) and then cast Mulch or Wood Elves to develop their board. Playing a land and casting Mulch (with the untapped lands available after land drop) would advance their game plan much more meaningfully. If they want to cast Wood Elves and then equip Greaves to protect it, they need to unequip from Meren first anyway, but the equip should come after deploying creatures, not before.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Lightning Greaves equip for 0 before playing a land or casting any spells.
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest (or Golgari Guildgate), then cast Mulch to find more lands and fill the graveyard for Meren's ability, or cast Wood Elves to ramp. Equip Greaves later to protect a newly deployed creature.

annotations.description: Gem3Flash chose to equip Lightning Greaves to Meren (who is already on the battlefield and doesn't need haste) before casting any spells. They have Wood Elves in hand which costs 2G and they have access to the mana to cast it (Swamp untapped + Vivid Marsh could produce green). Wood Elves would fetch a Forest, fixing mana and ramping, and also trigger Meren's death/experience counter synergies later. More importantly, casting a creature first and then equipping Greaves to protect either Meren or the new creature would be better sequencing. However, looking at the mana more carefully: Command Tower is tapped, both Forests are tapped, one Swamp is tapped. Available mana is: Vivid Marsh (untapped, can produce B or any color by removing a charge counter) and Swamp (untapped, produces B). That's only 2 mana available, and Wood Elves costs 2G - they'd need at least one green. Vivid Marsh could produce G by removing a charge counter, giving them BG - but Wood Elves costs 2G (one generic + one green + one more generic), which is 3 total mana. They only have 2 mana available. So they actually can't cast Wood Elves this turn. Mulch costs 1G - that's 2 mana, one must be green. With Vivid Marsh removing a counter for G and Swamp for B, they have BG - enough for Mulch (1G). Viridian Zealot costs GG - they'd need two green, but only have one green source available. So the only castable spell is Mulch. Equipping Greaves first before casting Mulch is fine since Mulch is a sorcery and order doesn't matter much. But they should cast Mulch this turn to develop. If this is the only action they take (just equipping), that might waste the turn's mana. Actually, this is just the first action - they can still cast Mulch after equipping. The equip itself is free, so no mana is wasted. This seems reasonable.
annotations.actionTaken: Equipped Lightning Greaves (to Meren presumably) for 0 mana
annotations.betterLine: This is actually fine as a first action since equip costs 0; they can still cast Mulch afterwards with their remaining mana

Lightning Greaves gives shroud and haste, and equipping it to Meren (their commander and key value engine) protects her from targeted removal at zero cost. This is pure upside that was declined.

Playing a land first would leave more flexibility.

annotations.description: GPT-4.1-mini cast Duelist's Heritage before playing a land for the turn. They had Evolving Wilds and Azorius Chancery available as land drops. Playing a land first is standard sequencing - Evolving Wilds could be cracked immediately to thin the deck, and having the land in play before committing mana to spells ensures maximum flexibility.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Duelist's Heritage before making a land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Evolving Wilds first (crack it to fetch a basic), then cast Duelist's Heritage. This ensures the land drop isn't forgotten and gets deck thinning started immediately.

annotations.description: Playing Evolving Wilds before Azorius Chancery is slightly worse mana sequencing. Playing Azorius Chancery first (bouncing a tapped land like Island) would provide WU mana next turn, and then Evolving Wilds could be played the following turn. This order maximizes available mana sooner, which matters when trying to cast Cauldron of Souls (5 mana) or Citadel Siege (4 mana) as soon as possible.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Evolving Wilds as land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Azorius Chancery, bouncing a tapped land (e.g., Island), to get the double-mana bounce land online sooner and maximize mana development for casting 4-5 mana spells in hand.

annotations.description: GPT-4.1-mini passed on activating Crystalline Crawler's tap ability to add a free +1/+1 counter, which is pure upside costing nothing but tapping the creature. With Ishai as their key threat (growing from opponent spells), growing the Crawler for free is still value. Additionally, if Evolving Wilds was available untapped, fetching a land for free is also missed value.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating any abilities
annotations.betterLine: Tap Crystalline Crawler to put a +1/+1 counter on it (free value), and activate Evolving Wilds if available to thin the deck and fix mana

annotations.description: Casting Great Oak Guardian (a flash creature) during the precombat main phase rather than during combat or at end of opponent's turn wastes its flash advantage and the untap/pump trigger. The +2/+2 and untap effect is best used as a combat trick or surprise blocker. Additionally, casting it now gives GPT-4.1-mini's Ishai another counter unnecessarily before combat. Bloodspore Thrinax could have been a stronger play to set up future creatures entering with extra counters, especially with Meren on board for recurring creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Great Oak Guardian during precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Cast Bloodspore Thrinax (potentially devouring nothing for now to set up future synergy with Meren), or if wanting Great Oak Guardian, cast it during the declare attackers step to pump Meren for combat damage. Alternatively, play Golgari Rot Farm first to set up future mana, then consider casting Thief of Blood or Bloodspore Thrinax.

annotations.description: Chose Butcher of Malakir to return to hand when Thief of Blood would be much more impactful against the current board state. GPT-4.1-mini has Ishai (which accumulates +1/+1 counters from opponent spells) and Crystalline Crawler with counters. Thief of Blood would strip all those counters and become a huge flying threat. Additionally, Gem3Flash already has Terastodon competing for the expensive-creature slot in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Butcher of Malakir (7 mana) to return to hand via Meren
annotations.betterLine: Choose Thief of Blood (6 mana) to return to hand - it directly answers Ishai's counter accumulation and Crystalline Crawler, while being cheaper to cast than Butcher

annotations.description: Chose Terastodon (MV 8) with Meren's ability when they only have 7 lands and will likely need to discard to hand size. Terastodon costs 6GG which is far beyond their current mana. More immediately castable creatures like Acidic Slime (3GG - castable with current lands), Shriekmaw (evokable for 1B), or even Butcher of Malakir would provide more near-term value.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Terastodon with Meren's end step trigger to return to hand
annotations.betterLine: Target Shriekmaw (castable via evoke for 1B to kill Ishai) or Acidic Slime (castable at 3GG with current 7 lands) to get an immediately usable creature

annotations.description: Casting Vulturous Zombie triggers Ishai to grow larger, while Gem3Flash has Sever the Bloodline in hand which would exile Ishai (the only remaining opponent's key threat that grows with every spell cast). Each spell Gem3Flash casts makes Ishai more dangerous. Sever costs only 3B (4 mana) vs Vulturous Zombie's 3BG (5 mana), so Gem3Flash could have exiled Ishai and potentially cast another cheap creature like Viridian Zealot or Phyrexian Rager in the same turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Vulturous Zombie, growing Ishai by +1/+1 in the process
annotations.betterLine: Cast Sever the Bloodline targeting Ishai, Ojutai Dragonspeaker to exile GPT-4.1-mini's main threat, then use remaining mana for Viridian Zealot or Phyrexian Rager

annotations.description: Moving Lightning Greaves from Pathbreaker Ibex to Vulturous Zombie is suboptimal. Pathbreaker Ibex is the key threat multiplier that enables massive attacks, and Meren is the recursion engine. Vulturous Zombie is just an incremental grower and far less critical to protect.
annotations.actionTaken: Equipped Lightning Greaves to Vulturous Zombie, leaving Pathbreaker Ibex and Meren unprotected.
annotations.betterLine: Keep Lightning Greaves on Pathbreaker Ibex to protect the most impactful creature, or move it to Meren to protect the recursion engine.

annotations.description: Gem3Flash declined to activate Terramorphic Expanse, which is a free land search that provides ramp, deck thinning, and a land in graveyard (relevant for Centaur Vinecrasher in hand). There is no downside to cracking it postcombat.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate any abilities, passing without cracking Terramorphic Expanse.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Terramorphic Expanse to search for a basic land, gaining incremental advantage at no cost.

annotations.description: Gem3Flash passed without activating Terramorphic Expanse to fetch a basic land. Cracking a fetch land is essentially free value - it thins the deck and provides an additional land for future turns. With expensive cards in hand (Centaur Vinecrasher, Rise from the Grave, Sever the Bloodline) and Meren wanting more mana to operate, there's no reason not to activate it.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating any abilities
annotations.betterLine: Activate Terramorphic Expanse to search for a basic land, getting additional mana for future turns and thinning the deck

annotations.description: Lightning Greaves was equipped to Phyrexian Rager, a 2/2 with no ongoing value, instead of Meren of Clan Nel Toth, the commander and key engine piece that generates recurring value every end step. Meren's ability targets graveyard cards, not herself, so shroud doesn't interfere with her functionality.
annotations.actionTaken: Equipped Lightning Greaves to Phyrexian Rager (2/2)
annotations.betterLine: Equip Lightning Greaves to Meren of Clan Nel Toth to protect the most important creature on the board from removal.

annotations.description: Gem3Flash chose Terastodon as the Meren end-step target, but Terastodon costs 8 mana and Meren almost certainly doesn't have 8+ experience counters, so it just goes to hand. However, Terastodon is already in hand effectively useless without enough mana to cast it (only 8 lands, some tapped). Meanwhile, Eternal Witness was also available and was actually the card returned to hand. But looking more carefully at the 'After' field, Meren targeted Eternal Witness and returned it to hand — the system shows Terastodon was 'Chosen' but the resolution targeted Eternal Witness. Actually, re-reading: the choice was Terastodon, but the After shows Eternal Witness was targeted and returned. This is confusing. Let me re-read. The Chosen field says 'Terastodon' but the After says Meren targeted Eternal Witness. This likely means the system corrected or the choice of Terastodon was the initial selection but Meren resolved on Eternal Witness. Actually, looking at the choices list, Terastodon isn't even listed among the 10 shown choices (the list shows 14 but only 10 are displayed). Terastodon is in the graveyard so it should be a valid target. The choice of Terastodon over Eternal Witness is questionable - Eternal Witness can recur any card and costs only 3 mana (castable next turn), while Terastodon costs 8 mana and would be very hard to cast. But Terastodon is a powerful effect. Given the game state with only 2 opponents left (both eliminated at negative life?), getting Eternal Witness to recur a key spell seems better. Actually both Gemini2.5Flash and Devstral are at negative life, so only GPT-4.1-mini remains at 22hp. Eternal Witness could recur Pathbreaker Ibex or other key cards. But the After shows Eternal Witness was actually returned, so perhaps Terastodon was selected first and then Eternal Witness was the actual Meren target. This is confusing output. Given the choice shown was Terastodon, which is an 8-mana creature unlikely to be cast soon, while Eternal Witness at 3 mana provides immediate value, choosing Terastodon seems suboptimal.
annotations.actionTaken: Selected Terastodon as the Meren of Clan Nel Toth end-step graveyard target
annotations.betterLine: Select Eternal Witness (3 mana, castable next turn to recur a key card like Pathbreaker Ibex or Overwhelming Stampede) or Butcher of Malakir/Acidic Slime for immediate board impact

annotations.description: Equipping Lightning Greaves to Meren before casting any creatures gives Meren shroud prematurely. Since Greaves has Equip {0}, the correct sequence is to cast creatures first (like Korozda Guildmage for BG using Vivid Marsh + Swamp), then decide which creature gets the Greaves protection. Equipping first means they'd need to move Greaves off Meren (temporarily removing shroud) to cast and then re-equip, which creates a window of vulnerability.
annotations.actionTaken: Equipped Lightning Greaves to Meren of Clan Nel Toth before casting any other spells
annotations.betterLine: Cast Korozda Guildmage first using Vivid Marsh (removing charge counter for G) and Swamp (for B), then equip Lightning Greaves to whichever creature needs protection most

annotations.description: Gem3Flash likely doesn't have enough experience counters to return Butcher of Malakir (CMC 7) directly to the battlefield, so it will just go to hand. With only ~7-8 lands and many tapped, casting it next turn is difficult. A cheaper creature like Sakura-Tribe Elder or Eternal Witness (CMC 2-3) would more likely meet the experience counter threshold and enter the battlefield directly, providing immediate value - Sakura-Tribe Elder gives ramp and an experience counter on sacrifice, Eternal Witness recovers a key card.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Butcher of Malakir as the Meren end-step target, which likely just goes to hand as an expensive card they can't cast soon.
annotations.betterLine: Choose Sakura-Tribe Elder or Eternal Witness - creatures with low enough CMV to potentially return directly to the battlefield via Meren, providing immediate board impact and incremental advantage.

annotations.description: Centaur Vinecrasher would enter as approximately a 32/32 with trample (counting ~32 land cards across all graveyards) for only 4 mana, and could immediately be equipped with Lightning Greaves for haste+shroud to attack. Instead, Gem3Flash spent all 7 mana on a 5/4 Butcher of Malakir that can't attack this turn and also gives Ishai another counter.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Butcher of Malakir for 7 mana, deploying a 5/4 flyer with no immediate board impact.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Centaur Vinecrasher for 4 mana (entering as ~32/32 trample), equip Lightning Greaves for free (haste+shroud), and attack GPT-4.1-mini for lethal or near-lethal damage. Remaining 3 mana could be used for Viridian Zealot or held for Altar's Reap.

annotations.description: Equipping Lightning Greaves to Pathbreaker Ibex (3/3) instead of Vulturous Zombie (11/11). The Vulturous Zombie is the biggest threat on board and the creature that maximizes Pathbreaker Ibex's attack trigger (+11/+11 to all creatures). If an opponent removes the unprotected 11/11 Vulturous Zombie before combat, the Ibex trigger drops dramatically in value.
annotations.actionTaken: Equipped Lightning Greaves to Pathbreaker Ibex (3/3)
annotations.betterLine: Equip Lightning Greaves to Vulturous Zombie (11/11) to protect the biggest threat and ensure maximum value from Pathbreaker Ibex's attack trigger. Greaves can be moved to Ibex after attacks are declared if needed (equip 0).

annotations.description: Gem3Flash declined to activate Jarad, Golgari Lich Lord's graveyard ability to return it to hand by sacrificing a Swamp and a Forest. With 20+ creature cards in the graveyard, Jarad would enter as a massive creature and could use its drain ability to close out the game. The cost of two basic lands is relatively minor in this late-game state.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without activating any abilities
annotations.betterLine: Activate Jarad's graveyard ability, sacrificing a Swamp and a Forest to return Jarad to hand. Jarad would be enormous with all the creature cards in the graveyard and could potentially win the game with its sacrifice-drain ability.
